<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915066_theRebbe_447" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915066_theRebbe_447__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that "came with days" means all his days were complete and full in divine service, and distinguishes between service within measurement and limitation and the superior service of "zaken" that transcends measurement, connected to the thirteen rectifications of the beard.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">The explanation is,</t>
    <t s="1">that the meaning of "came with days" is</t>
    <t s="2">(as explained briefly in Torah Or27</t>
    <t s="3">and at length in Ohr HaTorah on our portion28)</t>
    <t s="4">that all his days were complete and supernal days, and not a single day was lacking, G-d forbid</t>
    <t s="5">(as brought in the Zohar29).</t>
    <t s="6">And this is the meaning of "came with days,"</t>
    <t s="7">that he came with all his days.</t>
    <t s="8">And this is the content of "came with days"</t>
    <t s="9">(in the verse "And Avraham and Sarah... came with days,"</t>
    <t s="10">and in the verse "And Avraham was old, came with days"),</t>
    <t s="11">that the sum total of his days until then were complete and full days in the service of G-d.</t>
    <t s="12">And within this itself there are two modes30,</t>
    <t s="13">that the service should be in the manner of "came with days" and the absence of lack,</t>
    <t s="14">but nevertheless this is within measurement and limitation,</t>
    <t s="15">of</t>
    <t s="16">his deficiency that is lacking to him.</t>
    <t s="17">However, above this is the service that is beyond measurement and limitation32,</t>
    <t s="18">"You are obligated to enrich him."</t>
    <t s="19">And this is the novel point of "And Avraham was old, came with days" beyond what is said "And Avraham and Sarah were old, coming with days,"</t>
    <t s="20">for the aforementioned verse</t>
    <t s="21">("And Avraham and Sarah...")</t>
    <t s="22">is the perfection of service within measurement and limitation</t>
    <t s="23">(for "old" there does not refer to the whiteness of the hairs),</t>
    <t s="24">but not so the verse "And Avraham was old, came with days" is the perfection of service of "old" that is beyond measurement and limitation.</t>
    <t s="25">And this is the matter of old age, which is the whitening of the hairs,</t>
    <t s="26">that refers to the hairs of the beard,</t>
    <t s="27">and is connected with the aspect of the supernal "old,"</t>
    <t s="28">the aspect of the beard of Atik Yomin,</t>
    <t s="29">which has thirteen rectifications of the beard, which are the thirteen attributes of mercy,</t>
    <t s="30">as above,</t>
    <t s="31">for the matter of the attributes of mercy is beyond measurement and limitation.</t>
    <t s="32">For hairs in general, their matter is the contraction of vitality,</t>
    <t s="33">to the point that the vitality is in a manner of complete cessation</t>
    <t s="34">(as explained in these discourses33),</t>
    <t s="35">and the novel point here is that the hairs are white in color,</t>
    <t s="36">which is connected with the thirteen rectifications of the beard,</t>
    <t s="37">the thirteen attributes of mercy,</t>
    <t s="38">completely beyond measurement and limitation.</t>
    <t s="39">And this is the novel point in what is said "And Avraham was old, came with days,"</t>
    <t s="40">that the matter of "came with days,"</t>
    <t s="41">the perfection of days,</t>
    <t s="42">that the days are full and complete,</t>
    <t s="43">is in the manner of "old" that is completely beyond measurement and limitation,</t>
    <t s="44">even to the manner of the thirteen rectifications of the beard.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the Torah is eternal and the service of Avraham applies to every Jew, especially through the prayer of the Avos blessing, and that the three modes of service (love, fear, mercy) are interincluded.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">Now, the Torah is eternal34,</t>
    <t s="1">and all the matters within it are eternal instructions for every single Jew,</t>
    <t s="2">and from this it is understood that this matter is an instruction in the service of every single Jew.</t>
    <t s="3">And especially since this matter pertains to Avraham Avinu, about whom our sages said35</t>
    <t s="4">"We call 'fathers' only the three,"</t>
    <t s="5">and it is explained in many places36</t>
    <t s="6">that the service of each of the tribes pertains primarily to that tribe,</t>
    <t s="7">and in general, Yisrael are divided into the two lines of Yissachar and Zevulun,</t>
    <t s="8">masters of Torah and masters of good deeds37,</t>
    <t s="9">but not so the service of the Avos, which pertains to every single Jew.</t>
    <t s="10">(From all this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="11">that the aforementioned service of Avraham Avinu</t>
    <t s="12">("old, came with days")</t>
    <t s="13">also exists in every single Jew).</t>
    <t s="14">And especially in the service of prayer, which every day we say at the beginning of the Amidah prayer the first blessing called "Birkas Avos"38,</t>
    <t s="15">and we conclude the blessing "Magen Avraham"</t>
    <t s="16">(meaning that this is the seal that authenticates the entire matter).</t>
    <t s="17">Moreover, this prayer is repeated three times each day,</t>
    <t s="18">and four times on Shabbos and Yom Tov, etc., and five times on Yom Kippur.</t>
    <t s="19">And this is why we conclude "Magen Avraham," because Avraham includes everything.</t>
    <t s="20">And this means,</t>
    <t s="21">that in addition to the three prayers in general being corresponding to the three Avos and were instituted by them39,</t>
    <t s="22">in more particularity there are three modes of service of the three Avos,</t>
    <t s="23">love, fear, and mercy40,</t>
    <t s="24">in the service of the entire day.</t>
    <t s="25">And as explained in many places41</t>
    <t s="26">that the attributes of holiness are interincluded with each other,</t>
    <t s="27">and even more particularly, according to what is explained in the discourses of Sefiras HaOmer42</t>
    <t s="28">that there is the interinclusion of each of the seven attributes within the seven,</t>
    <t s="29">from this it is understood all the more so regarding the three attributes of love, fear, and mercy, that they are interincluded with each other.</t>
    <t s="30">And this is the matter of "And Avraham was old, came with days" in service,</t>
    <t s="31">that just as in Avraham there was the matter of "came with days,"</t>
    <t s="32">complete days,</t>
    <t s="33">and the matter of "And Avraham was old,"</t>
    <t s="34">"old" meaning he acquired wisdom43,</t>
    <t s="35">and the matter of the thirteen rectifications of the beard,</t>
    <t s="36">the service beyond measurement and limitation as above,</t>
    <t s="37">and as explained at length in the maamar of the Baal HaYom HaHuledes mentioned above,</t>
    <t s="38">so too must all these matters be in the service of every single Jew.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section adds that the maamar was said over ninety years ago, and discusses the special completeness in Torah study and prayer that begins at ninety, the principle that a student's power is greater than the teacher's, and how this relates to the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And we may add to this,</t>
    <t s="1">that the aforementioned maamar of the Baal HaYom HaHuledes was said over ninety years ago</t>
    <t s="2">(5654).</t>
    <t s="3">And our sages said in the Mishnah in Avos44</t>
    <t s="4">"A son of ninety for bending"45,</t>
    <t s="5">that the matter of "bending" refers to the matter of prayer</t>
    <t s="6">(according to the interpretation of several commentators on the Mishnah in Avos there46),</t>
    <t s="7">and as it is also written in our portion47</t>
    <t s="8">"And Yitzchak went out to bend in the field,"</t>
    <t s="9">and our sages said39,</t>
    <t s="10">"There is no 'bending' except prayer,"</t>
    <t s="11">and likewise it refers to the matter of Torah study</t>
    <t s="12">(as stated in the commentators on the Mishnah46),</t>
    <t s="13">and as it is written in Tehillim in "Temanya Api"</t>
    <t s="14">(Psalm 11948)</t>
    <t s="15">"How I love Your Torah, all day it is my bending,"</t>
    <t s="16">and one can say the intention in this,</t>
    <t s="17">that from the age of ninety begins a special completeness in Torah study and the service of prayer.</t>
    <t s="18">And in the manner that our sages said49</t>
    <t s="19">"Until forty years a person does not stand on his teacher's mind,"</t>
    <t s="20">meaning that a special completeness in Torah study begins after forty years,</t>
    <t s="21">likewise a special completeness in the manner of understanding Torah, etc., begins after ninety years.</t>
    <t s="22">For it is simple that the intention is not that after he reaches the age of ninety he cannot ascend more and more,</t>
    <t s="23">rather the explanation is that in the ninetieth year a special elevation is added,</t>
    <t s="24">and within this itself one must ascend in holiness50</t>
    <t s="25">and increase it51</t>
    <t s="26">more and more</t>
    <t s="27">(in Torah study).</t>
    <t s="28">And likewise in the matter of the fortieth year,</t>
    <t s="29">that what our sages said "until forty years, etc." does not mean that when the fortieth year arrives he cannot ascend further,</t>
    <t s="30">rather that then a special elevation is added,</t>
    <t s="31">and within it one must ascend in holiness and increase it, etc.</t>
    <t s="32">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="33">that our sages said52</t>
    <t s="34">that students are called sons and the teacher is called a father,</t>
    <t s="35">and it is brought in the Gemara53</t>
    <t s="36">that "the power of the son is greater than the power of the father,"</t>
    <t s="37">meaning,</t>
    <t s="38">that even though whatever the son has is from the father,</t>
    <t s="39">and that the power of the son being greater is from the power of the father54,</t>
    <t s="40">nevertheless, there are in the father hidden matters that are not revealed in him</t>
    <t s="41">(to the point that it is possible they are in a concealment that is not in existence),</t>
    <t s="42">and they are revealed only in the son.</t>
    <t s="43">And this matter is halachically</t>
    <t s="44">(in halachah?),</t>
    <t s="45">that there are things</t>
    <t s="46">(halachos?)</t>
    <t s="47">in which the power of the son is greater than the power of the father.</t>
    <t s="48">And so it is also with students and a teacher,</t>
    <t s="49">that the students have the power to innovate matters in halachah that the teacher did not innovate,</t>
    <t s="50">meaning they were in concealment with him</t>
    <t s="51">(completely).</t>
    <t s="52">[For this is55</t>
    <t s="53">also the explanation of what our sages said56</t>
    <t s="54">"Whatever a diligent student will innovate in the future was all given to Moshe at Sinai"</t>
    <t s="55">(as the statement57</t>
    <t s="56">"Moshe received Torah from Sinai, etc." meaning that Moshe received the entire Torah),</t>
    <t s="57">for the matters that were transmitted through Moshe, some of them are in ultimate concealment,</t>
    <t s="58">and the diligent student innovates them,</t>
    <t s="59">reveals these matters].</t>
    <t s="60">For from all this the matter of "a son of ninety for bending" is understood,</t>
    <t s="61">that when the time of ninety years arrives, a special completeness begins in the manner of Torah study, etc.</t>
    <t s="62">And so it will be understood also regarding our maamar and the matters within it.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
